visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The closest structurally analogous context, azosemide, which shares the thiophen-2-ylmethyl motif and acidic ionizable groups, has an estimated absolute oral bioavailability of approximately 20.4% in fasted healthy humans, meeting the F >= 20% threshold.

All visible L1 experimental F outcomes in the transfer contexts are at or above 20% (e.g., bumetanide 0.66–0.95, mosliciguat 23.1%, levodopa 63–99%, tolbutamide 80–100%, warfarin nearly complete, 6-MNA 35–38%), so no affirmative low-F experimental evidence is available to support F < 20%.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability measurement for the query molecule is available in the visible records.
Transfer from azosemide is uncertain because the query has two carboxylic acids and an imidazole rather than azosemide's tetrazole/sulfonamide/chloro substitution.
The query-specific prior is based on physicochemical descriptors only; no measured permeability, solubility, or first-pass data are supplied.
content.decision_summary: The visible L1 experimental contexts all report F >= 20%, including the closest structural analog azosemide at ~20.4%; the descriptor-based query prior is an uncertain, unmeasured signal and is insufficient to affirm F < 20%. The transferable experimental direction therefore supports high, with low confidence due to imperfect structural transfer.
